title: Kill a broker
goal: acks=all was three lines of configuration in step 09. This step is what those lines buy. Run a three-node Redpanda, replicate every topic, kill a node mid-stream and count nothing missing — then remove the safety margin and watch the producer refuse loudly instead of losing quietly.
startWith: Step 09 finished; comfortable stopping and starting containers without ceremony.

newIdeas.plain: Each partition gets a leader plus followers on other brokers. Producers and consumers only ever talk to the leader; followers exist to take over. rf=3 is the standard for anything that matters.

The in-sync replicas are the copies that are caught up. acks=all waits for all of them, and min.insync.replicas=2 with rf=3 means one broker can die without either losing data or blocking writes. It is the margin, written down.

What a producer gets when the ISR falls below the minimum. It looks like an outage and is actually the system keeping its promise: better to refuse a write than accept one that only exists in one place.

Letting a stale follower become leader restores availability by silently discarding acknowledged writes. Off by default. For money, it stays off — that is availability traded for truth, and the answer here is always truth.

tasks.do: Grow the cluster to three nodes
tasks.why: Replication on one broker is a diagram. Everything in this step needs somewhere for the copies to live.
tasks.how: Extend the compose file to three Redpanda nodes, then recreate the events topics with rf=3 and min.insync.replicas=2. Recreating loses local dev history — fine here, and a good reminder that in production this decision is made before the first byte, not after.

blocks.label: infra: docker-compose.kafka3.yml — the shape of it
blocks.body:
# Three redpanda services: lf-redpanda-1/2/3, each with
#   --seeds redpanda-1:33145 (all pointing at node 1)
#   distinct ports mapped for kafka (9092/9192/9292) and admin
# The redpanda docs' three-node compose is the reference;
# copy it and rename to the lf- prefix.

blocks.label: Recreate the topic, replicated
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk topic delete ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1
docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk topic create ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1 \
  -p 6 -r 3 -c min.insync.replicas=2

check.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk cluster health
check.expect: Three brokers, all healthy, no leaderless partitions.

tasks.do: Kill a broker mid-stream and count
tasks.why: Ten in, ten out across a consumer restart was step 09. Ten in, ten out across a broker death is the same proof one layer down.
tasks.how: Start a steady stream of holds, stop the broker that leads some of the topic's partitions, and let the stream keep running. The producer retries onto the new leaders; the consumer barely notices. When it is over, count events in against notifications out.

blocks.label: Steady stream, then pull the plug
blocks.body:
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -X POST localhost:8081/api/v1/holds \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"accountId\":\"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111\",\"wallets\":[\"A-$i\"]}" > /dev/null
  sleep 0.2
done &
sleep 3 && docker stop lf-redpanda-2

blocks.label: Who leads now
blocks.body: docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk topic describe ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1 -p

check.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk group describe notification-service
check.expect: Lag drains to 0 and all 50 events were processed, despite a broker dying in the middle.

tasks.do: Remove the margin and watch it refuse
tasks.why: The failure mode of min.insync.replicas is the whole reason to set it. You want to have seen the refusal in dev, because in production it pages someone.
tasks.how: Set min.insync.replicas=3 on the topic — now every write needs every broker. Stop one broker and produce: the producer throws NotEnoughReplicas instead of accepting a write with no safety copy. Put it back to 2 and bring the broker up.

blocks.label: No margin, then a dead broker
blocks.body:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk topic alter-config \
  ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1 --set min.insync.replicas=3
docker stop lf-redpanda-3
# now place a hold and watch ledger-service's log

blocks.label: What the error means
blocks.body: NotEnoughReplicasException is the broker declining to lie. The write would have been acknowledged with nowhere safe to put a copy — for a ledger, refusing is the correct behaviour, and your producer's retries plus the outbox from step 10 mean nothing is lost while it waits.

check.run: docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk topic describe ledgerflow.ledger.wallet-hold.events.v1
check.expect: min.insync.replicas back at 2, all three brokers up, cluster healthy again.

proof.run:
docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk cluster health
docker exec -it lf-redpanda-1 rpk group describe notification-service
proof.expect: A broker died mid-stream and every acknowledged write is still there; with the margin gone, writes failed fast instead of failing silently.
proof.note: Keep the single-node compose for daily work — three nodes is for this step and for demos. Note in the README that the dev default trades this guarantee for convenience.

doneWhen: A broker dies mid-stream and in equals out; with min.insync.replicas at the full count, the producer refuses instead of losing — and you have seen both with your own eyes.

lessons.title: Scratch files keep the chaos scripts
lessons.teach: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Insert makes a scratch file. The 50-hold loop and the broker-kill sequence are scripts you will run a dozen times today and want next month for a demo — a scratch keeps them runnable and out of the repository.
lessons.fallbackTip: Keep the loops in scripts/ locally; don't commit them.
